audit_findings.title: Post-anchor 3Cloud acquisition is missing from the perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $728 million filed purchase price ($733 million escrowed at 2025-12-31); owner-earnings effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: FY2025 anchor OE excludes 3Cloud while the June 2026 cash balance, debt, and share count are post-close; acquired OE, integration costs, and incremental working-capital needs are absent from the forecast perimeter
audit_findings.evidence: On January 1, 2026, through the execution of a purchase agreement, we acquired 100 % ownership in 3Cloud, one of the largest independent Microsoft Azure services providers and a global leader in Azure-dedicated AI enablement solutions and products.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, not merely a possible future event. Omitting acquired earnings understates value, while omitting integration and reinvestment costs can overstate it. The June cash-and-STI bridge is post-payment, so the record does not demonstrate that the escrow is double-counted, but the missing operating contribution remains reasonably capable of affecting the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Construct a 3Cloud-only post-close OE bridge from 2026 revenue, operating costs, cash taxes, maintenance capex, working capital, and integration costs; confirm the $733 million escrow is excluded from June cash; then rerun all scenarios with a consistent current perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Current debt is paired with pre-borrowing interest expense
audit_findings.magnitude: $984 million computed increase in debt, from $576 million at 2025-12-31 to $1.560 billion at 2026-06-30; recurring after-tax OE reduction unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-level OE correctly retains interest expense, but the FY2025 anchor contains only $37 million of interest expense and does not contain the recurring interest on the additional 2026 borrowing
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 we had no outstanding balance under our revolving credit facility.
audit_findings.explanation: The capital-structure timing mismatch is demonstrated. Debt principal need not be deducted under the stated method, but the associated recurring after-tax interest must reduce future OE. Because the bear value of $62.83 is only $0.52 per share above the $62.31 market price, even a modest recurring omission could change the scenario conclusion; the filing does not provide enough borrowing-date and rate detail to quantify the full run-rate cost.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each 2026 borrowing by amount, date, benchmark, margin, and use of proceeds; calculate the normalized annual cash interest and tax shield; reduce forecast OE from the appropriate period and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Past-service benefit obligation bypassed net income and OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $147 million liability increase; $0.32 per share and 0.44% of the $33.552 billion base equity value if deducted dollar-for-dollar
audit_findings.mechanism: The past-service cost entered OCI and the defined-benefit liability rather than net income-based OE, so it must be represented either as a bridge liability or through normalized future benefit expense
audit_findings.evidence: As a result, during the fourth quarter of 2025, we recorded a one-time increase to our defined benefit liability for past service of $147 million, in "Other noncurrent liabilities" in our consolidated statement of financial position with a corresponding increase in "Accumulated other comprehensive income (loss)".
audit_findings.explanation: The $147 million obligation is demonstrated, but its filed scale is not material to the valuation conclusion. A conservative full bridge deduction would reduce bear value from $62.83 to about $62.51, still above the $62.31 price, and would reduce the $51.65 buy-below level by only about $0.23. Future amortization or benefit expense could already capture part of the cost, so an additional full deduction could also double count it.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 2026 funded status and expected future amortization of prior-service cost; document whether it is captured in projected OE, and make only the non-duplicative bridge or OE adjustment.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved employment class-action exposure could be material
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately 2,300 potential class members and $16 million of interim attorneys' fees and costs; ultimate damages unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Unaccrued compensatory damages, punitive damages, defense costs, and any uninsured portion would reduce cash or OE available to common shareholders
audit_findings.evidence: Beca use we cannot predict the number of individual plaintiffs who will proceed to the second phase, or the outcome of those cases, and in view of the appellate arguments regarding class certification, we are unable to reasonably estimate a possible loss or range of loss.
audit_findings.explanation: An adverse liability-stage verdict and the rebuttable presumption for participating class members are demonstrated, but participation, individualized damages, punitive awards, appeals, and insurance recovery remain unknown. The record therefore establishes a real downside exposure but cannot establish whether its probability-weighted value is material.
audit_findings.action: Develop probability-weighted participation and damages ranges from the litigation record, include remaining legal costs, map insurance limits and exclusions, and rerun the bridge with low, central, and high net-loss cases.

audit_findings.title: India tax disputes are not explicitly reconciled in the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $349 million filed 2016 claim versus a $365 million deposited asset at 2026-06-30; 2013 exposure and additional interest or penalties unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A recovery of the excluded tax deposit would increase the equity bridge, while losses exceeding that excluded asset, including interest, penalties, or the 2013 claim, would reduce equity value or future OE
audit_findings.evidence: In March 2018, the ITD asserted that it is owed an additional 33 billion Indian rupees ($ 367 million at the December 31, 2025 exchange rate) on the 2016 transaction.
audit_findings.explanation: The known 2016 claim is more than covered by the $365 million deposit, and that deposit is recorded in other noncurrent assets rather than the $1.051 billion cash-and-STI bridge. Thus, losing the known $349 million claim would principally consume an asset already excluded from value, while winning could add up to about $0.80 per share before tax or collection effects. Materiality remains unresolved because the 2013 demand and any excess interest or penalties are unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each dispute's principal, interest, penalties, deposits, and accounting location at June 2026; confirm none of the $365 million is in bridge cash; then model recovery of the deposit and any net liability exceeding it.

audit_findings.title: The OE series must normalize offsetting 2025 one-offs
audit_findings.magnitude: $390 million noncash tax charge and $62 million pretax property gain ($53 million after the filed $9 million tax effect); net potential OE understatement of $337 million if neither was normalized
audit_findings.mechanism: The tax charge depresses 2025 OE and the ten-year log-trend, while the property gain inflates them; the resulting trend anchor feeds every forecast year and terminal value
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease in net income was primarily driven by the one-time, non-cash income tax expense of $390 million related to the enactment of the OBBBA, partially offset by an increase in income from operations, including the $62 million gain on sale of property and equipment.
audit_findings.explanation: The one-offs are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not show whether the OE calculation removed them, so an actual error is not yet demonstrated. If both remain, the net $337 million understatement equals 14.2% of reported 2025 OE and is large enough to materially alter the trend anchor and scenario values; if only the property gain remains, value is overstated instead.
audit_findings.action: Produce the 2025 OE calculation from GAAP net income or operating cash flow through every adjustment, show separate removal of the $390 million tax charge and the $62 million gain with its $9 million tax effect, recompute the complete ten-year OE series and log-trend, and rerun all scenarios.
